facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Murphy Oil Corporation is both the registrant and the issuer of the notes, so its consolidated statements are the issuer's own and no parent or subsidiary perimeter has to be split out. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest argument against ready with limitations is the notes table itself: two debt tables disagree on the coupon of one series, and a reader who took the note's total-debt line at face value would understate year-end 2025 debt. The balance-sheet ties and the issuer's printed weighted average coupons limit that risk, because they show which reading each table supports. The view would weaken if the executed indentures contradict the filings' description of the notes, and it would strengthen if a supplemental indenture or rating notice explains the 2042 coupon. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest contrary evidence to a comfortable credit view is cash generation, not leverage: after USD 1,526.64 million of capital spending, dividends and distributions, adjusted free cash flow was negative USD 32.2 million for the nine months, and the 2026 recovery in EBITDA rests on realized prices that the filings describe as volatile and exposed to regional conflict. If prices fell back toward the 2025 level, EBITDA would drift toward the year-end 2025 figure of USD 1,191.7 million, net leverage would return to 0.85x or higher as net debt rose, and cover would fall toward 13.52x. The view would strengthen if capital spending came in below the guided range, or if the executed indentures show the notes rank equally with the revolver. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Financial policy favours shareholders over debt reduction, and management says so. The dividend was raised 7.69% to USD 0.35 per share in January 2026, nothing has been repurchased since USD 100.0 million was bought in the first quarter of 2025 with USD 550 million still authorised, and the issuer states that adjusted free cash flow is more likely to go to repurchases than to bond repayment. Gross debt rose USD 249.27 million, or 18.00%, in nine months, to USD 1,634.35 million, because the 2034 notes added USD 272.51 million net of redemptions and the Vietnam finance lease USD 82.07 million, partly offset by the USD 100.0 million revolver repayment. Performance share awards vest 80% on relative shareholder return and 20% on return on capital employed, with no leverage measure, so leverage will fall through earnings and not through repayment. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The notes' place in the structure cannot be read from the filings, and the evidence points to a possible gap. The revolver has three named borrowers and two subsidiary guarantors, while each indenture in the exhibit index is between Murphy Oil Corporation and a trustee alone. If the notes carry no subsidiary guarantee, noteholders would rank behind revolver lenders at the operating subsidiaries that hold the assets; this is an unverified reading that the executed documents would settle. facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest case against a benign view of owner conduct is that distributions already exceed what the business keeps after investment: dividends of USD 150.5 million took 75.40% of free cash flow, adjusted free cash flow after distributions and acquisitions was negative USD 32.2 million, management prefers repurchases to bond repayment, and the Gulf of America minority drew more than it earned in 2024 and 2025. If oil fell back toward USD 66.70, those payments would come from cash or the revolver while exploration and drillship spending continue. The view would weaken if the proxy statement shows a large holder or an insider-heavy board, or if the debt documents allow wide restricted payments and the notes lack subsidiary guarantees. It would strengthen if the documents limit distributions as leverage rises, guarantee the notes alongside the revolver and show an independent board. Basis: calculation C6; calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 84–85, 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 50, 53

facts.label: Bottom line
facts.text: Murphy's credit profile is solid on leverage and liquidity but exposed to the oil price and thin on free cash flow, so creditors are well covered through a price fall like 2025's but not if shareholder returns and exploration spending keep rising. Net debt of USD 1,134.05 million is 0.65x last-twelve-month EBITDA, liquidity of USD 2,499.9 million is 152.96% of total debt and no note falls due before 2029, yet free cash flow was only USD 240.61 million after USD 1,526.64 million of property additions and no oil is hedged. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14, 55

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage is low and cover is wide, but both rest on an EBITDA that rose with price and not with volume. Last-twelve-month EBITDA of USD 1,740.6 million is 46.06% above FY2025 while third-quarter production was 7% lower, so net leverage of 0.65x and cash interest cover of 20.17x would read 0.95x and 13.81x if EBITDA returned to its FY2025 level of USD 1,191.7 million with debt unchanged; that is a sensitivity, not a forecast. The issuer's EBITDA excludes the minority in the Gulf of America venture while debt and cash include it, so the ratios are slightly conservative. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

facts.text: Margins are high but they follow price. EBITDA margin was 55.77% over the last twelve months against 44.30% in FY2025, helped by a 27.87% fall in lease operating expenses in the nine months, while exploration expenses rose 170.38% and depreciation, depletion and amortization 6.82%. Basis: calculation C2; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 37

facts.label: Contrary evidence and what would change the view
facts.text: The strongest evidence against a solid view is cash generation, not leverage: at 2025 prices adjusted free cash flow was USD 12.1 million, 2026 capital spending is running 16.98% above 2025 even at higher prices, and the 2026 EBITDA recovery rests on prices that the issuer calls volatile and exposed to a regional conflict. If WTI averaged USD 66.70 again, the illustration shows a USD 405.48 million annual gap and net leverage of 1.29x after one year, with USD 494.1 million of capitalised exploratory costs exposed to impairment, so the credit would drift weaker without any refinancing event. The view would weaken if adjusted free cash flow stays negative for another quarter while dividends rise or repurchases restart, or if capital spending guidance moves above USD 1,600 million; it would strengthen if capital spending came in below the guided range of USD 1,500 million to USD 1,600 million, if adjusted free cash flow stayed positive after dividends and minority distributions at lower prices, or if the notes proved to be guaranteed alongside the revolver. Basis: calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 51–52

facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario is a sustained oil price at the 2025 level of about USD 66.70, against USD 85.79 in the third quarter of 2026, which is 22.25% lower. The first operational break is revenue, because no oil is hedged and offshore fields supply 58.97% of sales; EBITDA then moves toward its FY2025 level of USD 1,191.7 million while capital spending stays near the last-twelve-month level and the dividend near USD 200.74 million a year. On that arithmetic, which is an illustration and not a forecast, the cash gap is USD 405.48 million a year before working capital and minority distributions, net leverage reaches 1.29x after one year and liquidity of USD 2,499.9 million covers the gap for 6.17 years, so no maturity falls inside the cover. Management can pause repurchases, cut the dividend, defer exploration and adjust capital spending, which makes liquidity distress unlikely before 2029; the observable triggers are negative adjusted free cash flow for a second quarter, WTI below USD 66.70 and any revolver drawing. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Murphy presents an adequate business profile supported by long reserve life, two oil basins plus Canadian gas and a low debt burden, but credit quality is constrained by an unhedged oil price, concentration in offshore hubs and thin free cash flow after a rising capital programme. Cash-flow durability appears adequate at current prices and weaker at 2025 prices, because adjusted free cash flow was USD 12.1 million in 2025. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access for new notes before the 2029 maturity and on whether the notes rank equally with the revolver. The primary downside path is a sustained price fall into a larger capital programme and fixed distributions. Further analysis would require a credit rating, the executed indentures and credit agreement, the proxy statement and unit cost data by field. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C8; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)

The run settings supply no ratings, quotes, peers, portfolio or legal documents and are not issuer evidence.

## Findings
### Bottom line

The seven supplied filings and releases support financial, business and fundamental credit work on Murphy Oil Corporation through the third quarter of 2026, with limitations; they cannot support covenant, structural or legal conclusions for creditors.

The evidence is current to the day before the as-of date, and the debt and liquidity inputs tie to each other across documents. Four source conflicts stay open for the next modules to carry rather than settle: the coupon of the 2042 notes, the label on total debt, the perimeter of the issuer's earnings measures, and the 2025 comparatives in the segment note. The executed indentures and credit agreement, any credit rating, and the 2026 proxy statement are not supplied, so the guarantee and security status of the notes, covenant definitions and headroom, and board independence are not established.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C4; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 83–85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14
### Key findings

Murphy Oil Corporation is both the registrant and the issuer of the notes, so its consolidated statements are the issuer's own and no parent or subsidiary perimeter has to be split out. The one perimeter difference is the noncontrolling interest in the Gulf of America joint venture: the issuer's earnings measures exclude it, while its consolidated balance sheet, cash and liquidity totals include it, so a ratio built from the issuer's earnings measure and its consolidated debt would mix two perimeters.

The evidence runs from the audited 2025 annual report to the quarterly report for the period ended September 30, 2026, signed on November 4, 2026, one day before the as-of date. Nothing supplied is dated after the as-of date. The post-quarter items that matter to creditors, a drillship agreement signed in October 2026, new exploration blocks, a Mauritania agreement and amended by-laws, are disclosed in documents signed on or before November 4, 2026.

Debt and liquidity inputs are printed in every filing and agree with the balance sheet: the debt note, counting the revolver line printed beneath its total, equals current plus long-term debt on the balance sheet at year-end 2025 and at September 30, 2026, the notes table sums to its printed total, and the issuer's liquidity statement reproduces from cash, the undrawn revolver and the letters of credit drawn on it. Series-level debt tables are printed only at those two dates; the March and June 2026 filings describe the same refinancing in narrative.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14, 47

Four conflicts are open and are carried forward unsettled. The coupon of the 2042 notes is printed three ways, and the issuer's own weighted average coupons point to a change between the first and second quarters of 2026 that no document explains. The line labelled total debt in the debt note leaves out the revolver printed beneath it, so it differs from the balance sheet at year-end 2025. The 2025 comparatives in the segment note differ slightly from the statement of operations. The issuer's earnings measures and its debt use different perimeters.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 83, 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14

Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit are each ready with limitations. ### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest argument against ready with limitations is the notes table itself: two debt tables disagree on the coupon of one series, and a reader who took the note's total-debt line at face value would understate year-end 2025 debt. The balance-sheet ties and the issuer's printed weighted average coupons limit that risk, because they show which reading each table supports. The view would weaken if the executed indentures contradict the filings' description of the notes, and it would strengthen if a supplemental indenture or rating notice explains the 2042 coupon.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C6; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13

## Request

MURPHY OIL CORP (Murphy Oil Corporation, issuer id mur), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot: the financial foundation (statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics) built from the supplied filings and releases through the third quarter of 2026.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Financial foundation shows low leverage and ample liquidity at September 30, 2026: net debt of USD 1,134.05 million is 0.65x last-twelve-month EBITDA, but free cash flow is thin because capital spending absorbs most operating cash flow.

Total debt is USD 1,634.35 million against liquidity of USD 2,499.9 million, EBITDA covers cash interest 20.17x, and no note falls due before 2029. The ratios use the issuer's EBITDA measure, which excludes a noncontrolling interest that debt and cash include, so they are slightly conservative; two source conflicts remain open, the 2042 notes coupon and the total debt label. The 2026 rise in EBITDA reflects higher realized prices, and free cash flow over the last twelve months is USD 240.61 million after USD 1,526.64 million of capital spending.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C5; calculation C6; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 45, 47
### Key findings

Net debt rose from USD 1,007.88 million at year-end 2025 to USD 1,134.05 million at September 30, 2026, yet net leverage fell from 0.85x to 0.65x because last-twelve-month EBITDA rose from USD 1,191.7 million to USD 1,740.6 million. Total debt grew by USD 249.27 million: the January 2026 refinancing added USD 272.51 million of notes net of redemptions, finance leases rose USD 82.07 million with the Vietnam floating storage vessel lease, and repaying the USD 100.0 million revolver borrowing offset part of it. Taken alone, the largest event after year-end is the dividend paid on March 2, 2026, which lifts year-end net debt to USD 1,058.06 million, or 0.89x.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C15; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–15, 32

The rise in EBITDA came from higher realized prices in the United States and Canada and lower lease operating expenses, partly offset by lower volumes, and it lifted cash interest cover from 13.52x at year-end 2025 to 20.17x. Cash interest paid is steady at about USD 86.31 million over the last twelve months, so cover moves with EBITDA and not with the cost of debt. On the issuer's adjusted measure, which also adds back asset retirement accretion, leverage is 0.92x gross and 0.64x net.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C12; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 45, 49

Cash-flow quality is the weak point. Capital spending absorbed 48.92% of last-twelve-month revenue, so free cash flow was only 0.14x EBITDA, and the issuer's own adjusted free cash flow, after dividends, distributions to the noncontrolling interest and acquisitions, was negative USD 32.2 million for the nine months. Cash still rose over the nine months because the refinancing raised more than it repaid, so a fall in prices would reach net debt quickly while dividends and a capital programme guided at USD 1,500 million to USD 1,600 million for the year remain to be funded.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45–46, 52; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_mur-2026q3xex991.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10

Liquidity is USD 2,499.9 million, or 152.96% of total debt: USD 500.3 million of cash and USD 1,999.6 million undrawn on the USD 2,000.0 million revolver, which expires in January 2031. No note principal falls due before 2029, and the larger series fall due in 2032, 2034 and 2042. The total of letters of credit outstanding is stated only at year-end 2025, so liquidity is net only of the USD 0.4 million drawn on the revolver.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 47; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 74, 113

Four definition and source conflicts are logged. The issuer's EBITDA excludes the noncontrolling interest while consolidated debt and cash include it, and on a consolidated house-derived basis net leverage is 0.61x against 0.65x, so the reported ratio is the more conservative. The note line labelled total debt omits the revolver printed beneath it. The 2042 notes carry different coupons in the 2025 annual report and the third quarter report, and the issuer's weighted average coupons imply the change fell between the first and second quarters of 2026. The 2025 comparatives in the segment note differ from the statement of operations by up to USD 2.4 million.
Basis: calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C14; Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 112–113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14, 48

No non-debt funding float is stated: the filings show no supplier finance, factoring, deferred revenue or customer deposits. An October 2026 agreement for a deepwater drillship, with initial-term consideration of USD 225 million to USD 325 million gross, is not recognised in the statements and is kept out of period figures, as are the exploration items announced after the quarter.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 34
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest contrary evidence to a comfortable credit view is cash generation, not leverage: after USD 1,526.64 million of capital spending, dividends and distributions, adjusted free cash flow was negative USD 32.2 million for the nine months, and the 2026 recovery in EBITDA rests on realized prices that the filings describe as volatile and exposed to regional conflict. If prices fell back toward the 2025 level, EBITDA would drift toward the year-end 2025 figure of USD 1,191.7 million, net leverage would return to 0.85x or higher as net debt rose, and cover would fall toward 13.52x. The view would strengthen if capital spending came in below the guided range, or if the executed indentures show the notes rank equally with the revolver.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 50–52; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_mur-2026q3xex991.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10
### Limitations
Interim cash flow statements are cumulative from January 1, so discrete second and third quarter cash flows are not shown and last-twelve-month figures use the reported year-to-date stubs.
The debt stack ranks only the revolver, because no source states the legal rank of the notes, and series-level debt tables are printed only at year-end 2025 and September 30, 2026.
Last-twelve-month ratios combine consolidated debt with an EBITDA that excludes the noncontrolling interest.
Basis: calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49

## Gaps

- The coupon of the 2042 notes is printed as 5.875% in the 2025 annual report debt table and as 6.375% in the third quarter report for both December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2026, and the 0.5 percentage points are worth about USD 1.70 million of interest a year on USD 339.761 million; this restricts the rate field of the 2042 notes. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the supplemental indenture or a rating notice, and show each date as printed until then.

- The security, guarantors and legal rank of the notes are not stated in any supplied document, so the debt stack ranks only the revolver and no secured or senior subtotal is stated. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the executed indentures.

- The revolver commitment at December 31, 2024 is not stated in the supplied filings, so undrawn committed facilities and liquidity are not supplied for FY2024. Severity: Medium. Action: supply the 2024 annual report or restate the 2024 liquidity from it.

- No series table of debt is printed at March 31 and June 30, 2026, so contractual principal, and the principal to carrying value reconciliation, is drawn at September 30, 2026 only. Severity: Medium. Action: build the interim principal from the September table and the events of the first quarter if it is needed.

- Total letters of credit outstanding is stated only at year-end 2025, at USD 211.8 million, while later filings state only the USD 0.4 million drawn on the revolver, so liquidity is not net of other letters of credit at interim dates. Severity: Medium. Action: obtain the figure from the issuer.

- The issuer's EBITDA measures exclude the noncontrolling interest in MP GOM while debt, cash and liquidity are consolidated, which restricts the comparability of every ratio; the house-derived consolidated sensitivity is in the calculation register. Severity: Medium. Action: label the perimeter wherever a ratio is quoted.

- Lines printed as dashes in the statements, such as impairment in the nine months of 2026 and derivative gains, are recorded as not supplied rather than zero, and lines that the interim statements do not print, such as purchased natural gas sales and costs, are not supplied for those periods. Severity: Low. Action: none needed unless a figure is used in a ratio.

- Interim cash flow statements are cumulative, so discrete second and third quarter cash flows and the fourth quarter of 2025 are not shown; the last-twelve-month figures use the reported year-to-date stubs. Severity: Low. Action: construct quarters only if a quarterly view is needed.

- Cash taxes paid are stated only in the annual report, and the sources do not split capital spending between maintenance and growth. Severity: Low. Action: carry total property additions and dry hole costs only.

- The balance sheet at December 31, 2023 is not in the supplied filings, so the balance sheet table starts at December 31, 2024. Severity: Low. Action: supply the 2024 annual report if a third year is needed.

- The 2025 comparatives in the segment note exceed the statement of operations by USD 2.2 million for the second quarter, USD 2.2 million for the six months, USD 0.2 million for the third quarter and USD 2.4 million for the nine months; the statement of operations is used. Severity: Low. Action: none.

- An October 2026 drillship agreement with initial-term consideration of USD 225 million to USD 325 million gross had not commenced at September 30, 2026 and is excluded from the statements and the net debt table. Severity: Low. Action: carry it as a post-period commitment when the next filing is read.
- The adjusted EBITDA bridge is drawn for FY2025 only, and interim bridges are not tabulated. Severity: Low. Action: use the issuer's quarterly reconciliations if an interim bridge is needed.
- No restricted cash is stated in the sources, so none is assumed and cash is shown as printed. Severity: Low. Action: none.

## Request

MURPHY OIL CORP (Murphy Oil Corporation, issuer id mur), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot: the business, ownership, transaction and governance facts that matter to creditors, taken from the supplied filings and releases through the third quarter of 2026. The run settings supply no ratings, quotes, peers or legal documents and are not issuer evidence.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Murphy Oil is a publicly listed producer with no sponsor or controlling holder named in the supplied documents, so creditors' risk lies in oil price exposure, offshore concentration and shareholder-return policy, not in owner conduct. Oil supplied 86.07% of sales revenue in the nine months to September 30, 2026 and offshore fields 58.97%, while dividends of USD 150.5 million took 75.40% of free cash flow and adjusted free cash flow, after dividends, minority distributions and acquisitions, was negative USD 32.2 million.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 50

Governance quality is thinly evidenced, because the proxy statement and the executed debt documents are not supplied, so board independence, large holders and any subsidiary guarantee of the notes are not established.
### Key findings

The one ownership fact that moves creditor risk is the 20% minority in the Gulf of America venture, which shares in the venture's earnings and takes cash out of it. The minority's share of nine-month net income is 13.54%, and its distributions ran at 1.50x its earnings in 2024, 1.85x in 2025 and 0.30x in the first nine months of 2026, when they were USD 21.16 million. Murphy reports 100% of the venture, so consolidated cash and liquidity include value that belongs to the minority while the issuer's earnings measures exclude it, and the documents do not name the minority holder.
Basis: calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 83, 96–97; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 37

The business is oil-weighted and concentrated, so cash flow follows one price and a few hubs. Oil was 86.07% of nine-month 2026 sales revenue against 82.81% in 2025, offshore fields supplied 58.97% against 61.21%, and ten fields give about 91% of Gulf of America output, which is about 65% of U.S. output. Chevron took 19% and ExxonMobil 12% of 2025 sales, no oil derivative was open at September 30, 2026, so price falls reach cash flow directly, and the Gulf of America storm season runs from June to November.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C9; calculation C14; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 27, 140; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9, 55

Earnings strength in 2026 comes from price, not volume. Third-quarter production was 7% below a year earlier on natural declines in the Gulf of America and the timing of new Eagle Ford wells, while WTI averaged USD 85.79 a barrel against USD 64.93 and the forward curve on November 2, 2026 stood at USD 96.46 for the rest of 2026 and USD 86.12 for 2027. Management raised full-year production guidance, but a return of oil toward the USD 66.70 average of the first nine months of 2025 would remove the cushion with lower volumes.
Basis: calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 38, 50, 52

Financial policy favours shareholders over debt reduction, and management says so. The dividend was raised 7.69% to USD 0.35 per share in January 2026, nothing has been repurchased since USD 100.0 million was bought in the first quarter of 2025 with USD 550 million still authorised, and the issuer states that adjusted free cash flow is more likely to go to repurchases than to bond repayment. Gross debt rose USD 249.27 million, or 18.00%, in nine months, to USD 1,634.35 million, because the 2034 notes added USD 272.51 million net of redemptions and the Vietnam finance lease USD 82.07 million, partly offset by the USD 100.0 million revolver repayment. Performance share awards vest 80% on relative shareholder return and 20% on return on capital employed, with no leverage measure, so leverage will fall through earnings and not through repayment.
Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 77, 121; 10-Q_2026-03-31_mur-20260331.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 53

Fixed commitments are building ahead of cash flow. A finance lease for the Vietnam storage vessel added a USD 83.9 million liability running to 2039, a drillship agreement signed in October 2026 commits USD 225 million to USD 325 million gross from 2027 and is not yet on the balance sheet, and capitalised exploratory costs awaiting a reserves decision rose from USD 191.8 million to USD 494.1 million, an increase of 157.60% that carries dry-hole and impairment risk. Nine-month capital spending took 86.98% of operating cash flow before working capital, and full-year capital spending is guided at USD 1,500 million to USD 1,600 million.
Basis: calculation C10; calculation C12; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 32, 50, 52

The notes' place in the structure cannot be read from the filings, and the evidence points to a possible gap. The revolver has three named borrowers and two subsidiary guarantors, while each indenture in the exhibit index is between Murphy Oil Corporation and a trustee alone. If the notes carry no subsidiary guarantee, noteholders would rank behind revolver lenders at the operating subsidiaries that hold the assets; this is an unverified reading that the executed documents would settle.

Reported governance shows nothing adverse, but it is thinly evidenced. The audit committee is made up only of non-employee directors, internal control over financial reporting was effective at the end of 2025, no restatement required recoupment, and the chief executive in office since January 2025 was promoted from President and Chief Operating Officer. The Board amended its By-Laws on November 4, 2026 and the text is not supplied, so the effect on creditors is not established.

One source conflict touches the revenue mix and none changes a conclusion. The segment note for 2025 totals about USD 2.4 million more than the statement of operations, which extends the nine-month difference found in Source readiness to the full year and corrects nothing in it, and the revenue mix uses lines that agree. Production differs by 0.29% between two tables because one counts production and the other sales.
Basis: calculation C11; Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 94, 141; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38–39
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest case against a benign view of owner conduct is that distributions already exceed what the business keeps after investment: dividends of USD 150.5 million took 75.40% of free cash flow, adjusted free cash flow after distributions and acquisitions was negative USD 32.2 million, management prefers repurchases to bond repayment, and the Gulf of America minority drew more than it earned in 2024 and 2025. If oil fell back toward USD 66.70, those payments would come from cash or the revolver while exploration and drillship spending continue. The view would weaken if the proxy statement shows a large holder or an insider-heavy board, or if the debt documents allow wide restricted payments and the notes lack subsidiary guarantees. It would strengthen if the documents limit distributions as leverage rises, guarantee the notes alongside the revolver and show an independent board.
Basis: calculation C6; calculation C8; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 84–85, 96; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 50, 53
### Limitations

- The proxy statement is not supplied, so board independence, committee membership, beneficial ownership and executive pay are not established; the conclusion that no controlling holder exists holds only for what the cover page, holder count and signatures show, and a large block would reverse it.

- The executed indentures, supplemental indentures and credit agreement are not supplied, so subsidiary guarantees of the notes and limits on distributions are not established; the ranking reading in the key findings could reverse.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 84–85
- Customer shares are printed for 2025 only, so the 31% concentration may not describe 2026 and the conclusion on customer dependence rests on a year-old split.
Basis: calculation C9; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 140
- Reserves are stated at the end of 2025 while the revenue mix covers nine months of 2026, so the reserve life of 10.60 years takes no account of 2026 production or exploration results.
Basis: calculation C4; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9

- The terms and costs of the new exploration positions are not stated, so the capital that exploration will absorb after 2026 cannot be estimated and the cash-use conclusions rest on 2026 guidance alone.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 52; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_mur-2026q3xex991.htm.jsonl, page 3
### Company and operating model

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The only new debt issue in the period is USD 500.0 million of 6.50% senior notes due February 15, 2034, closed on January 23, 2026 with USD 8.3 million of issuance costs. The proceeds redeemed the remaining USD 78.9 million of 2027 notes and USD 148.6 million of 2028 notes, USD 227.5 million in all, repaid the USD 100.0 million drawn on the revolver and covered fees, with the rest for general purposes, so notes principal rose a net USD 272.51 million and the nearest note maturity moved to 2029.
Basis: calculation C7; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 77, 114–115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 15

The USD 2.00 billion senior unsecured revolving credit facility was amended on January 2, 2026, raising capacity from USD 1.35 billion and extending maturity from October 2029 to January 2031. Three Murphy companies are named as borrowers and two subsidiaries as guarantors in the exhibit index, the margin spread adjustment fell from 0.10% to zero, USD 12.3 million of costs are being amortised, and at September 30, 2026 nothing was drawn and USD 0.4 million of letters of credit reduced capacity. Covenant levels after the amendment are not established, because the executed credit agreement is not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 85, 113–114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14; Source readiness (CP-0)

Two commitments sit outside the debt figure. The Vietnam storage vessel finance lease began in September 2026 and runs to October 2039, matching the production sharing contract, with a USD 83.9 million liability after USD 19.5 million was paid before commencement. A drillship agreement signed in October 2026 covers ten wells at USD 225 million to USD 325 million gross for the initial term, with options for up to five more, and starts in the first quarter of 2027, so nothing was recognised at September 30, 2026. In the first quarter of 2025 Murphy bought the Pioneer production vessel for USD 125.0 million, and the seller runs it under a five-year contract.
Basis: calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14, 32

Portfolio moves are small and exploratory. Murphy signed a Petroleum Agreement in January 2026 for an operated 75% interest in a Moroccan deepwater block with no firm wells in its first three years, secured six Gulf of America blocks in the August federal lease sale, signed two Mauritania blocks after the quarter and is finalising four in Cameroon, with costs not stated. Acquisitions of oil and gas properties were USD 28.6 million in the nine months of 2026 against USD 24.4 million a year earlier, and the 2025 Eagle Ford purchases and minor sale carry no stated consideration. No acquisition of a business or change of control appears in the documents.
The 2042 notes are carried at different coupons in the annual report and the third-quarter report, an open conflict from Source readiness, so that series is named by maturity only.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13
### Events: Issuer history

spans.text: # Fundamental credit for MURPHY OIL CORP (mur), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

MURPHY OIL CORP (Murphy Oil Corporation, issuer id mur), as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot: the overall fundamental credit view, drawn from the supplied filings and releases through the third quarter of 2026 and from the accepted modules on source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance. The run settings supply no ratings, quotes, peers or legal documents and are not issuer evidence.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Murphy's credit profile is solid on leverage and liquidity but exposed to the oil price and thin on free cash flow, so creditors are well covered through a price fall like 2025's but not if shareholder returns and exploration spending keep rising. Net debt of USD 1,134.05 million is 0.65x last-twelve-month EBITDA, liquidity of USD 2,499.9 million is 152.96% of total debt and no note falls due before 2029, yet free cash flow was only USD 240.61 million after USD 1,526.64 million of property additions and no oil is hedged.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C3; calculation C5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14, 55
The view is limited because no rating, peer data or executed debt document is supplied, so the profile is judged on its own terms and the ranking of the notes against the revolver is not tested.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 84–85
### Key findings

Leverage is low and cover is wide, but both rest on an EBITDA that rose with price and not with volume. Last-twelve-month EBITDA of USD 1,740.6 million is 46.06% above FY2025 while third-quarter production was 7% lower, so net leverage of 0.65x and cash interest cover of 20.17x would read 0.95x and 13.81x if EBITDA returned to its FY2025 level of USD 1,191.7 million with debt unchanged; that is a sensitivity, not a forecast. The issuer's EBITDA excludes the minority in the Gulf of America venture while debt and cash include it, so the ratios are slightly conservative.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 35

Margins are high but they follow price. EBITDA margin was 55.77% over the last twelve months against 44.30% in FY2025, helped by a 27.87% fall in lease operating expenses in the nine months, while exploration expenses rose 170.38% and depreciation, depletion and amortization 6.82%. A price fall would remove the revenue side of that gain at once, whereas the cost side rests on lower workover and production-related costs in the Gulf of America that may not repeat.
Basis: calculation C2; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 37

Cash conversion is the weakest dimension. Free cash flow of USD 240.61 million is only 0.14x EBITDA because property additions take 48.92% of revenue, nine-month capital spending is already 16.98% above the whole of 2025, and adjusted free cash flow after dividends, minority distributions and acquisitions was negative USD 32.2 million for the nine months. In 2025, at lower prices, adjusted free cash flow was USD 12.1 million, USD 87.9 million short of the USD 100.0 million of repurchases, and the revolver was drawn USD 100.0 million at the year end.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 45, 50; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 64, 113

Liquidity and the maturity profile remove refinancing risk for several years. Liquidity of USD 2,499.9 million is 152.96% of total debt and 3.48x the notes due through 2032; the first note maturity is USD 117.58 million in 2029, then USD 600.0 million in 2032, USD 500.0 million in 2034 and USD 339.76 million in 2042, and the USD 2.00 billion revolver is undrawn to January 2031. The notes average 8.4 years to maturity and the January 2026 issue of USD 500.0 million at 6.50% shows market access, but no rating is supplied, so the cost of the next refinancing is not established.
Basis: calculation C5; calculation C6; Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13–14; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_mur-2026q3xex991.htm.jsonl, page 2

The primary downside is a sustained fall in oil into a larger capital programme and fixed shareholder returns, and it would be met from liquidity before it reached a maturity. On the illustration in the downside scenario below, cash flow at its 2025 level against current property additions and dividends leaves a gap of USD 405.48 million a year, which liquidity covers for 6.17 years while net leverage rises to 1.29x after one year; the first observable breaks would be negative adjusted free cash flow for a second quarter and WTI below USD 66.70.
Basis: calculation C8; calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 38, 50

Business concentration widens the range around that path. Oil is 86.07% of nine-month sales revenue, offshore fields supply 58.97%, ten fields give about 91% of Gulf of America output and two customers took 31% of 2025 sales, so an outage or a lost buyer would hit a large share of cash flow with no hedge to cushion it.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11

Financial policy leans to shareholders and the structure of the notes is unverified. Dividends took 75.40% of free cash flow, management says adjusted free cash flow is more likely to go to repurchases than to bond repayment, and the sponsor and governance risk level is Medium; the revolver has two subsidiary guarantors while the indentures name only the parent, so the notes may rank behind revolver lenders at the operating subsidiaries, which the executed documents would settle.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 84–85; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 53

Three source conflicts remain open and none changes the view: the 2042 notes coupon differs between the annual report and the third-quarter report, the issuer's earnings measures exclude the minority while debt and cash include it, and the 2025 segment note differs from the statement of operations by about USD 2.4 million. The maturity amounts and ratios above do not depend on how they resolve.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; calculation C11
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a solid view is cash generation, not leverage: at 2025 prices adjusted free cash flow was USD 12.1 million, 2026 capital spending is running 16.98% above 2025 even at higher prices, and the 2026 EBITDA recovery rests on prices that the issuer calls volatile and exposed to a regional conflict. If WTI averaged USD 66.70 again, the illustration shows a USD 405.48 million annual gap and net leverage of 1.29x after one year, with USD 494.1 million of capitalised exploratory costs exposed to impairment, so the credit would drift weaker without any refinancing event. The view would weaken if adjusted free cash flow stays negative for another quarter while dividends rise or repurchases restart, or if capital spending guidance moves above USD 1,600 million; it would strengthen if capital spending came in below the guided range of USD 1,500 million to USD 1,600 million, if adjusted free cash flow stayed positive after dividends and minority distributions at lower prices, or if the notes proved to be guaranteed alongside the revolver.
Basis: calculation C4; calculation C7; calculation C8; calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 51–52
### Limitations

- No credit rating, market quote or peer data is supplied, so the profile cannot be set against typical leveraged-credit issuers or the market's pricing, and the overall view is absolute rather than relative.
Basis: Source readiness (CP-0)

- The downside arithmetic applies FY2025 EBITDA and cash flow to current debt and the last-twelve-month capital programme and omits working capital, minority distributions and management action, so it sizes the exposure and does not forecast it.
Basis: calculation C8

- Lease operating expense per barrel is supplied for the three quarters of 2026 but not for 2025, and field decline rates are not supplied at all, so margin resilience at lower prices rests on the 2025 EBITDA outcome and not on a cost model by field.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-06_mur-2026q1xex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_mur-2026q2xex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_mur-2026q3xex991.htm.jsonl, page 1
- Covenant levels are known only from the summary of the previous revolver, so the leverage and cover reference levels in the monitoring triggers carry no covenant headroom.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 113; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Strengths and weaknesses

Liquidity is the strongest support. Cash of USD 500.3 million plus the undrawn USD 2.00 billion revolver, less USD 0.4 million of letters of credit, gives USD 2,499.9 million, 152.96% of total debt, so a cash gap of the size in the downside illustration can be carried for several years without a maturity or a market window.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C5; calculation C8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 14

Low leverage and a long maturity profile support debt service. Net debt is 0.65x EBITDA, EBITDA covers cash interest 20.17x and the notes average 8.4 years to maturity with no principal due before 2029, so interest and refinancing take little of earnings and the next call on cash flow is far away.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C6; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_mur-2026q3xex991.htm.jsonl, page 2

Reserves give the asset base time. Proved reserves of 730.0 million barrels of oil equivalent equal 10.60 years of 2025 production, Lac Da Vang began producing in the third quarter of 2026 and Chinook #8 is online, so cash flow has development projects behind it and not only depletion.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9

Spending is discretionary, which gives management levers. No shares were repurchased in the nine months of 2026, planned capital expenditure may be adjusted during the year and exploration is guided at USD 195 million, so cash can be preserved before liquidity falls.

### Company description

Murphy is an independent oil and gas producer whose cash flow comes mainly from oil sold at index prices from the Gulf of America, the Eagle Ford Shale and Canadian offshore fields, with Canadian onshore gas as the second source and an exploration programme in Vietnam, Côte d'Ivoire, Morocco and new countries. Oil is 86.07% of nine-month 2026 sales revenue and offshore fields 58.97%, so visibility depends on the oil price and a few hubs; reserves equal to 10.60 years of production give the longer visibility that debt service needs.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–9
### Ownership and group structure

Murphy is a listed company with no sponsor or controlling holder named in the supplied documents. Its operating subsidiaries are wholly owned except for a 20% minority in the Gulf of America venture, whose share of nine-month net income is 13.54% and which drew more than it earned in 2024 and 2025. The revolver is guaranteed by two subsidiaries while the notes are issued by the parent, so their structural ranking is not established, and financial policy leans to shareholders, with a sponsor and governance risk level of Medium.
Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 84–85
### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Revenue is price-taking. Sales are largely index-priced, no oil is hedged and Canadian fixed-price forward sales cover only part of the gas, so the rise in WTI from USD 64.93 to USD 85.79 in the third quarter, while production fell 7%, explains the revenue gain. Two customers took 31% of 2025 sales, but the issuer sees no difficulty selling at market prices because many purchasers exist, so buyer concentration is a lesser risk than price.
Basis: calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 38, 53; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 140–141
### Cost structure and margin resilience

Margin follows price, and this year's cost gains came from lower workover and production-related costs. EBITDA margin was 55.77% over the last twelve months against 44.30% in FY2025, lease operating expense was USD 8.20 per barrel of oil equivalent in the third quarter against USD 8.70 and USD 8.83 in the first two, and nine-month lease operating expenses fell 27.87% on lower workover and production-related costs in the Gulf of America, while depreciation, depletion and amortization rose 6.82%. Margins can be defended against modest volume loss, but not against a price fall to the 2025 level, where EBITDA was USD 1,191.7 million.

Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 35, 37; EX-99.1_2026-05-06_mur-2026q1xex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-08-05_mur-2026q2xex991.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_mur-2026q3xex991.htm.jsonl, page 1
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

Capital intensity is the main constraint on cash conversion. Property additions are 48.92% of revenue, full-year capital spending is guided at USD 1,500 million to USD 1,600 million excluding the minority, and the Vietnam lease and the drillship add fixed calls, so EBITDA converts to only 0.14x of free cash flow. The issuer states that planned capital expenditure may be adjusted during the year, which is a lever, but it is exercised against committed drilling and a capitalised exploratory balance of USD 494.1 million.
Basis: calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 32, 52
### Industry forces

Competitive rivalry is limited because Murphy is a price taker in a commodity market; the force that matters is price, set by supply decisions that the issuer says it cannot predict. New entrants are not a credit factor given the capital needed. Substitutes and climate policy act through long-run demand, which the annual report lists as a risk, and are not a primary driver within 24 months. Buyer power is small because sales are index-priced and many purchasers exist, though two customers took 31% of 2025 sales. Supplier power shows in drilling rigs, vessels and operators: the drillship agreement and the five-year operating contract on the Pioneer vessel commit Murphy to those suppliers' rates and capacity for the contract terms.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 32, 51; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 140–141; calculation C11
### Political and economic factors

Political and economic factors are material, and social and technological factors are not a primary credit driver on the documents supplied. The regional conflict involving Iran affects prices and equipment costs through the Strait of Hormuz, new tariffs of 10% or 12.5% on imports from 60 economies add cost uncertainty, and offshore regulation in the Gulf of America covers well design, well control and subsea containment; the issuer has had no direct disruption, but lower prices or higher costs could cause material impairment charges, which links the political risk to the capitalised exploratory balance.
### Opportunities and threats

Opportunities that could improve credit quality are the ramp-up of Lac Da Vang and Chinook #8, the Cello and Banjo discoveries expected to produce in the fourth quarter of 2027 and the Bubale appraisal programme, all of which add volume that existing cash flow can fund if prices hold. Threats that could weaken it are a fall in WTI toward USD 66.70, a storm in the Gulf of America, dry holes on new exploration positions and the restart of repurchases while adjusted free cash flow is negative. Strengths and weaknesses are set out above.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 34, 52; calculation C9; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_mur-2026q3xex991.htm.jsonl, page 2
### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 months to 24 months the tailwinds are forward prices of USD 96.46 for the rest of 2026 and USD 86.12 for 2027 and raised production guidance, and the headwinds are that spending steps up, with the drillship starting in the first quarter of 2027, a decision on Hai Su Vang expected in late 2027 and exploration expense guided at USD 195 million. Over three to five years the 2029 notes of USD 117.58 million are the first maturity, the revolver matures in January 2031 and the Vietnam lease runs to 2039, so the funding profile is long while the sector headwind is a price that the issuer cannot control.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 32, 38, 50, 52; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_mur-2026q3xex991.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation C6
### Downside scenario

The scenario is a sustained oil price at the 2025 level of about USD 66.70, against USD 85.79 in the third quarter of 2026, which is 22.25% lower. The first operational break is revenue, because no oil is hedged and offshore fields supply 58.97% of sales; EBITDA then moves toward its FY2025 level of USD 1,191.7 million while capital spending stays near the last-twelve-month level and the dividend near USD 200.74 million a year. On that arithmetic, which is an illustration and not a forecast, the cash gap is USD 405.48 million a year before working capital and minority distributions, net leverage reaches 1.29x after one year and liquidity of USD 2,499.9 million covers the gap for 6.17 years, so no maturity falls inside the cover. Management can pause repurchases, cut the dividend, defer exploration and adjust capital spending, which makes liquidity distress unlikely before 2029; the observable triggers are negative adjusted free cash flow for a second quarter, WTI below USD 66.70 and any revolver drawing.
Basis: calculation C1; calculation C8; calculation C9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_mur-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 38, 50, 52; 10-K_2025-12-31_mur-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 64
### Overall credit view

Overall, Murphy presents an adequate business profile supported by long reserve life, two oil basins plus Canadian gas and a low debt burden, but credit quality is constrained by an unhedged oil price, concentration in offshore hubs and thin free cash flow after a rising capital programme. Cash-flow durability appears adequate at current prices and weaker at 2025 prices, because adjusted free cash flow was USD 12.1 million in 2025. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on market access for new notes before the 2029 maturity and on whether the notes rank equally with the revolver. The primary downside path is a sustained price fall into a larger capital programme and fixed distributions. Further analysis would require a credit rating, the executed indentures and credit agreement, the proxy statement and unit cost data by field.
Basis: calculation C7; calculation C8; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0)
